title: Three-trial handgrip sequence shape and stair difficulty: an exploratory cross-cohort prediction test
abstract: We tested whether curvature and interhand change disagreement in six existing grip trials add to conventional strength and demographics for concurrent stair difficulty. NHANES2011–2012 provided 1160 adults aged60+ for training; independently recruited2013–2014 provided 1235 for frozen evaluation. Adding grip-sequence curvature and interhand slope disagreement changed cross-cohort Brier score from 0.116410 to 0.116226 (difference -0.000184; joint PSU-bootstrap95% interval -0.001592 to +0.003815). The registered improvement criterion was not met; this does not establish equivalence or absence of physiological information. Both cohorts were previously inspected for other questions, not untouched confirmation. Independent-study-program validation remains incomplete.
